title: How to have great conversations, with Charles Duhigg and Michael Yeomans, PhD

sentences.en: You probably know what it feels like when a conversation just clicks.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道当谈话产生共鸣时是什么感觉。

sentences.en: You and the person you're talking to understand each other.
sentences.zh: 你和谈话对象彼此理解。

sentences.en: They're not just listening to you, they're hearing what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是在听你说话，而是在真正听懂你的意思。

sentences.en: You leave the conversation feeling good.
sentences.zh: 谈话结束后，你会感觉很好。

sentences.en: Maybe you sparked a new friendship, or deepened an old one, or figured out how to solve a problem that's been bothering you.
sentences.zh: 也许你们擦出了友谊的火花，加深了旧情，或者找到了解决困扰已久问题的办法。

sentences.en: Conversational chemistry might seem intangible, something that just happens when the circumstances are right.
sentences.zh: 谈话的化学反应似乎是无形的，仿佛只是在特定情况下自然发生的。

sentences.en: But psychologists, using new research tools and methods, are beginning to figure out what makes some conversations work, while others fall flat.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家利用新的研究工具和方法，开始弄清楚是什么让一些谈话奏效，而另一些谈话却冷场。

sentences.en: And their insights can help people improve their conversation skills, strengthen their relationships, and even disagree in more productive ways.
sentences.zh: 他们的见解可以帮助人们提高谈话技巧，巩固人际关系，甚至以更具建设性的方式处理分歧。

sentences.en: So what makes conversations click?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让谈话产生共鸣呢？

sentences.en: Why are some people so much better at verbal communication than others?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人比其他人更擅长口头交流？

sentences.en: What role does listening play in conversation?
sentences.zh: 倾听在谈话中扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: And how can you learn to listen better?
sentences.zh: 你该如何学会更好地倾听？

sentences.en: Why is it important to think about your goals in a conversation and to consider your partner's conversation goals as well?
sentences.zh: 为什么思考你在谈话中的目标，并考虑对方的谈话目标很重要？

sentences.en: What's the best way to build rapport with someone you just met?
sentences.zh: 与刚认识的人建立融洽关系的最好方法是什么？

sentences.en: How can you disagree productively without having the conversation spiral into an argument?
sentences.zh: 如何才能在不让谈话演变成争吵的情况下进行建设性的意见分歧？

sentences.en: And what are the most important things you can do to improve your conversation skills?
sentences.zh: 提高谈话技巧最重要的几件事是什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Michael Yeomans, an assistant professor of strategy and organizational behavior at Imperial College in London.
sentences.zh: 第一位是伦敦帝国理工学院战略与组织行为学助理教授迈克尔·约曼斯博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Yeomans has a PhD in behavioral science from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, and was previously a postdoctoral fellow at the Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 约曼斯博士拥有芝加哥大学布斯商学院的行为科学博士学位，此前曾是哈佛商学院的博士后研究员。

sentences.en: His research uses an artificial intelligence method called natural language processing to analyze conversations to understand and improve how people communicate with one another.
sentences.zh: 他的研究利用一种称为自然语言处理的人工智能方法来分析谈话，以理解并改善人们之间的沟通方式。

sentences.en: He's interested in how people make decisions in conversations and how we can make those decisions better.
sentences.zh: 他关注人们如何在谈话中做出决策，以及我们如何能做出更好的决策。

sentences.en: Next is Charles Duhigg, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and author.
sentences.zh: 下一位是普利策奖得主、记者兼作家查尔斯·杜希格。

sentences.en: His new book to be published in February 2024 is called Super Communicators, How to Unlock the Secret Language of Connection, and it's all about the science of conversation.
sentences.zh: 他将于2024年2月出版的新书名为《超级沟通者：如何解锁连接的秘密语言》，全书探讨的正是谈话的科学。

sentences.en: Mr. Duhigg has written for The New Yorker magazine and The New York Times, among other publications.
sentences.zh: 杜希格先生曾为《纽约客》杂志和《纽约时报》等刊物撰稿。

sentences.en: He is also the author of two bestselling books, The Power of Habit about habit formation, and
sentences.zh: 他还是两本畅销书的作者，一本是关于习惯养成的《习惯的力量》，另一本是

sentences.en: Smarter, Faster, Better about the science of productivity.
sentences.zh: 关于生产力科学的《更聪明、更快、更好》。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 感谢两位今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: We've all met people who seem to be naturally great at conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们都遇到过天生就非常擅长谈话的人。

sentences.en: They can connect with anyone.
sentences.zh: 他们能与任何人建立联系。

sentences.en: Charles, in your book, you call people like the super communicators.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯，你在书中把这类人称为“超级沟通者”。

sentences.en: So why don't we start there?
sentences.zh: 那我们从这里开始吧？

sentences.en: Who are these super communicators?
sentences.zh: 这些超级沟通者是谁？

sentences.en: And do you have any really great examples?
sentences.zh: 你有什么非常好的例子吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think actually all of us know super communicators, and oftentimes we are super communicators ourselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我认为我们每个人都认识超级沟通者，而且很多时候我们自己就是超级沟通者。

sentences.en: If I was to ask everyone listening to think of the person that you would call if you were having a bad day, the person you know that would make you just feel better, kind of listen
sentences.zh: 如果我让每一位听众去想一个你在心情不好时会打电话给的人，那个你知道会让你感觉好起来的人，那种会

sentences.en: to you exactly the right way, everyone listening would have someone pop into their mind.
sentences.zh: 以恰当的方式倾听你的人，每个人脑海中都会浮现出一个人选。

sentences.en: And that person, for you, is a super communicator.
sentences.zh: 对你来说，那个人就是超级沟通者。

sentences.en: They know how to listen.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何倾听。

sentences.en: They know how to show they're listening.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何表现出自己在倾听。

sentences.en: They know how to speak in ways that it's easier for you to listen.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何以让你更容易听进去的方式说话。

sentences.en: And we all have these moments in our own lives when we know exactly the right thing to say to a friend to make them feel better, or we know exactly what to say during a meeting
sentences.zh: 我们生活中都有这样的时刻：我们知道对朋友说些什么能让他们感觉好起来，或者我们知道在会议中该说些什么

sentences.en: in order to get everyone on board with our idea.
sentences.zh: 才能让大家支持我们的想法。

sentences.en: It's not a magical power, is the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这并不是什么魔法。

sentences.en: It's a set of skills that some people have learned a little bit better that recognize more.
sentences.zh: 这是一套有些人学得更好、运用得更多的技能。

sentences.en: But they're skills that all of us can learn, instincts that all of us have, that if we're reminded how to use them, we can communicate with anyone.
sentences.zh: 但这些是我们所有人都能学会的技能，是我们所有人与生俱来的本能，只要提醒自己如何使用，我们就能与任何人沟通。

sentences.en: Now, Mike, you don't use that term in your work, the term super communicators, but do you come across people like this in your studies?
sentences.zh: 迈克，你在工作中不使用“超级沟通者”这个词，但在你的研究中会遇到这样的人吗？

sentences.en: And what are they doing that the rest of us aren't?
sentences.zh: 他们做了什么而我们其他人没做到的？

sentences.en: Yeah, Kim, I think it's a great term.
sentences.zh: 是的，金，我认为这是一个很棒的词。

sentences.en: I come across them in my studies.
sentences.zh: 我在研究中确实会遇到他们。

sentences.en: And if I'm lucky, I come across a few in my life every once in a while, too.
sentences.zh: 如果幸运的话，我生活中偶尔也会遇到几个。

sentences.en: I think Charles describes it really aptly, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为查尔斯的描述非常贴切，对吧？

sentences.en: These are people who understand their conversation partner.
sentences.zh: 这些人了解他们的谈话对象。

sentences.en: They understand the goals they want to achieve and what their partner wants to achieve and
sentences.zh: 他们了解自己想要实现的目标以及对方想要实现的目标，并且

sentences.en: have the skills, have the adeptness, the quickness, and the sensitivity to be able to build a conversation from turn to turn over time so that it actually adds up to something much
sentences.zh: 拥有技能、敏锐度、反应速度和感知力，能够随着时间的推移，一轮接一轮地构建谈话，使之最终汇聚成比单纯交流言语

sentences.en: bigger than that, right?
sentences.zh: 更有意义的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Not just exchanging words, but meeting of minds.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是交换言语，而是思想的碰撞。

sentences.en: And I think Charles also makes a really good point about the nature of the relationship, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为查尔斯关于关系本质的观点也非常好，对吧？

sentences.en: Like so often when we are at our conversational best, it's because we're with people we understand well, we know their patterns, we know what they're looking for, we maybe share
sentences.zh: 就像我们谈话表现最好的时候，往往是因为我们和那些我们非常了解的人在一起，我们知道他们的模式，知道他们在寻找什么，也许还和他们分享

sentences.en: a sense of humor with them.
sentences.zh: 同样的幽默感。

sentences.en: And there's a bit of a filtering of who we end up talking to, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我们最终与谁交谈是经过筛选的，对吧？

sentences.en: We tend to seek out the people we've had good experiences with before.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于寻找那些以前有过良好互动体验的人。

sentences.en: But I think we can learn from those situations the kinds of skills and tools that can be useful more broadly.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们可以从这些情况中学习到更广泛适用的技能和工具。

sentences.en: And a lot of what the real super communicators do, the people who are good like this with
sentences.zh: 而真正的超级沟通者，那些能与所有人进行良好沟通的人，他们所做的很多事情就是

sentences.en: everybody, is that they understand how to adapt their toolkit to the needs in the context in front of them.
sentences.zh: 理解如何根据眼前的需求和情境来调整自己的工具箱。

sentences.en: One thread that runs through the work that both of you do is the importance of understanding that there are many different kinds of conversations and conversational goals.
sentences.zh: 你们两人的工作贯穿的一条主线是：理解存在许多不同类型的谈话和谈话目标非常重要。

sentences.en: Why is it important to understand your own goals and your partner's goals in conversation?
sentences.zh: 为什么理解自己和对方在谈话中的目标很重要？

sentences.en: Well, in many ways, a conversation is all about the goals, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在很多方面，谈话的核心就是目标，对吧？

sentences.en: We oftentimes enter into a conversation with a specific objective in mind, although we might not be aware of that objective ourself.
sentences.zh: 我们进入谈话时往往带着特定的目标，尽管我们自己可能并未意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I've really loved about doing this research, including Mike's research and many of his colleagues, is that as we learn more about how communication works
sentences.zh: 关于这项研究，包括迈克的研究和他许多同事的研究，我真正喜欢的一点是，随着我们对沟通运作方式了解的加深

sentences.en: within our minds, we've learned that there are different kinds of conversations, right?
sentences.zh: 我们认识到谈话有不同的类型，对吧？

sentences.en: And in particular, it seems like there's sort of three big buckets that we can put a lot of conversations into.
sentences.zh: 特别是，似乎我们可以把很多谈话归入三大类。

sentences.en: There's conversations that are practical, right?
sentences.zh: 第一类是实用型谈话，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to decide where we're going to dinner tonight or what we should do about the fact that Jimmy can't get his homework in on time.
sentences.zh: 我想决定今晚去哪里吃饭，或者我们该如何处理吉米不能按时交作业的问题。

sentences.en: Or I want to talk about, you know, what we should do as we get older.
sentences.zh: 或者我想讨论一下，你知道，随着年龄增长我们该怎么办。

sentences.en: And that's kind of a conversation about like, what are we really talking about?
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种关于“我们到底在谈论什么”的谈话。

sentences.en: What do we want to figure out here?
sentences.zh: 我们想在这里弄清楚什么？

sentences.en: But then there's other types of conversations where the goal is not to come up with a plan or to use reason to figure things out.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他类型的谈话，其目的不是制定计划或运用理性来解决问题。

sentences.en: It's just to share with you how I feel.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了与你分享我的感受。

sentences.en: And those are emotional conversations where what we're talking about is, is how do I feel?
sentences.zh: 那些是情感型谈话，我们谈论的是“我感觉如何”。

sentences.en: And then another big bucket are social conversations, discussions where I am sharing who I am from an identity perspective, from a background perspective, based on my experiences.
sentences.zh: 另一个大类是社交型谈话，即我从身份、背景和经历的角度分享我是谁的讨论。

sentences.en: I want to learn who you are based on where you come from and what you believe in.
sentences.zh: 我想根据你的出身和信仰来了解你是谁。

sentences.en: And that's really a social conversation, a conversation about who are we.
sentences.zh: 那确实是社交型谈话，关于“我们是谁”的谈话。

sentences.en: And what's important is that a lot of the research shows if I come into a conversation and I'm talking
sentences.zh: 重要的是，许多研究表明，如果我进入一场谈话，而我正在谈论

sentences.en: about emotions, if I come home from work one day and I've had a tough day and I'm telling my wife
sentences.zh: 情感，比如我有一天下班回家，度过了艰难的一天，我正在告诉我的妻子

sentences.en: all about my boss who's a jerk and my coworkers don't appreciate me, and my wife responds with
sentences.zh: 关于我那个混蛋老板和不赏识我的同事，而我的妻子回应我

sentences.en: some very good practical advice, like why don't you take your boss to lunch and get to know him a little bit better?
sentences.zh: 一些非常好的实用建议，比如“你为什么不请你老板吃午饭，多了解他一点呢？”

sentences.en: Even though she's trying to be supportive, even though that's very good advice, it's unlikely I'm going to hear it, right?
sentences.zh: 即使她是在试图支持我，即使那是很好的建议，我也很可能听不进去，对吧？

sentences.en: We've all been in this situation where I'm having an emotional conversation and she's having a practical conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们都经历过这种情况：我正在进行情感型谈话，而她正在进行实用型谈话。

sentences.en: And as a result, we don't connect.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们没有建立连接。

sentences.en: We don't hear each other.
sentences.zh: 我们没有听懂对方。

sentences.en: We both walk away a little bit frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我们两人最后都感到有点沮丧。

sentences.en: So I think one of the big things that I've carried away from reviewing this research is it's important to have the same kind of conversation at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从回顾这些研究中我学到的重要一点是：在同一时间进行同一种类型的谈话非常重要。

sentences.en: And that means understanding what your own goal is and what other people's goals are in a discussion.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要理解自己在讨论中的目标，以及对方的目标是什么。

sentences.en: So Mike, does that mean that people need to announce to each other what they want to talk about, what the purpose of the conversation is?
sentences.zh: 那么迈克，这是否意味着人们需要向对方宣布他们想谈论什么，谈话的目的是什么？

sentences.en: Does that make you a better conversationalist?
sentences.zh: 这会让你成为一个更好的谈话者吗？

sentences.en: I think a little bit of announcing could be helpful.
sentences.zh: 我认为稍微宣布一下可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: I also think a little bit of asking could be helpful too, right?
sentences.zh: 我也认为稍微询问一下也会有帮助，对吧？

sentences.en: There's many parties involved.
sentences.zh: 这涉及多方参与。

sentences.en: I mean, I think those three categories are, it's a nice way of thinking about the different types of conversations we might hope to achieve.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为那三个类别是一个很好的思考方式，可以用来思考我们可能希望实现的各种谈话类型。

sentences.en: And it's tricky because every conversation could be a mix of a few of them, right?
sentences.zh: 这很棘手，因为每一场谈话都可能是其中几种类型的混合，对吧？

sentences.en: And because every relationship you have is a series of conversations over time, right?
sentences.zh: 而且因为你拥有的每一段关系都是随着时间推移的一系列谈话，对吧？

sentences.en: So you need to be able to apply and know when to apply the skills at the right time.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要能够应用这些技能，并知道何时在正确的时间应用它们。

sentences.en: You know, I think some people don't know their own goals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为有些人甚至不知道自己的目标。

sentences.en: You know, business scholars will do these studies where people write down their objectives for like, you know, the next year at work or the next five years of their life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，商业学者会做这些研究，让人们写下他们对工作未来一年或人生未来五年的目标。

sentences.en: And you'd be surprised how often people miss common objectives, even just describing their own goals.
sentences.zh: 你会惊讶地发现，人们经常忽略共同目标，甚至在描述自己的目标时也是如此。

sentences.en: And I think the same is true of conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为谈话也是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: Simply listing the goals you might have before a conversation to be clear of what those are, right?
sentences.zh: 在谈话前简单列出你可能有的目标，以明确这些目标是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: And maybe even thinking through some of the topics you might cover when you're talking with somebody can only hope, I think,
sentences.zh: 甚至思考一下当你与某人交谈时可能会涉及的一些话题，我认为这只能

sentences.en: to help you achieve those goals merely by identifying them, but also doing a bit of cognitive offloading
sentences.zh: 帮助你实现这些目标，不仅是通过识别它们，而且还可以进行一点认知卸载，

sentences.en: in the sense that rather than having to do the cognitive work of trying to think what you're trying
sentences.zh: 意思是说，与其在试图实现目标的同时还要进行思考“我试图实现什么”的认知工作，

sentences.en: to achieve as you're trying to achieve it, by just putting a little bit of preparation,
sentences.zh: 只要提前做一点准备，

sentences.en: you know, in advance, then the actual conversation will flow a lot smoother.
sentences.zh: 那么实际的谈话就会流畅得多。

sentences.en: And I think the same is also true about preparing to understand your partner.
sentences.zh: 我认为在准备理解你的伴侣方面也是如此。

sentences.en: Now, you don't know exactly what their goals are yet either, but you can at least have a plan to learn what those goals are.
sentences.zh: 现在，你还不知道他们的确切目标，但你至少可以有一个计划去了解那些目标是什么。

sentences.en: I think Mike brings up a really important point here, which is that oftentimes a conversation that we have is not just one conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为迈克在这里提出了一个非常重要的观点，那就是我们进行的谈话往往不仅仅是一场谈话，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not just talking about emotions or just talking about social topics.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅仅是在谈论情感或仅仅谈论社交话题。

sentences.en: We move from conversation to conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们会在不同的谈话之间转换。

sentences.en: And what's important is that our partner is able to recognize as we're moving from topic to topic and is inviting us to join them in a certain kind of conversation.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，我们的伴侣能够在我们从一个话题转换到另一个话题时识别出来，并邀请我们加入他们进行某种特定的谈话。

sentences.en: And one of the things that really strikes me is that when we are in those conversations, oftentimes we are announcing our goals, right?
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的一点是，当我们进行那些谈话时，我们往往是在宣布我们的目标，对吧？

sentences.zh: 一个人看某样东西，我们也看同样的东西，对吧？
